title: Out of memory after data growth
story: Batch size grows from 60 to 180 MiB after 20 s; the 128 MiB limit OOM-kills every job. Expected heal: raise memory.

args.summary: Raised worker memory limit from 128m to 256m to accommodate the 180 MiB batch jobs that were causing repeated OOM kills, well within the 512m per-service and 1g total guardrails.

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: Repeated OOM kills (exit 137) on the 128 MiB memory limit once the job plan's batch size stepped up from 60 MiB to 180 MiB at t=20s (`JOB_PLAN=0:60,20:180`): logs show "job 11: loading batch (180 MiB)" immediately followed by "Killed process 9468 (rss 130 MiB > limit 128 MiB)", then repeated restarts all dying at rss 130-135 MiB against the 128 MiB limit — pure memory exhaustion, not CPU (cpu_pct_avg_total only 1.6%, peak 7.0%).

CHANGE: Raised the worker's memory limit from 128m to 256m (set_memory, the only allowed action), giving enough headroom above the observed ~135 MiB OOM-kill RSS for the 180 MiB batch stage; replicas stay at 1 (stateful=false but max_replicas=1, jobs not partitioned) and cpus untouched since there's no CPU pressure.

GUARDRAILS: Dry run passed with no violations — 256m ≤ max_memory 512m and ≤ max_total_memory 1g at replicas=1; allowed_actions includes set_memory only, which is what was changed; image/environment left untouched per policy.

FOLLOW-UP: Monitor the next few nightly runs for mem_peak_mb against the new 256m limit — if the batch size plan grows again (e.g., a future larger tier beyond 180 MiB), the memory limit will need another bump; consider also alerting if mem_peak_mb exceeds ~70% of the limit to catch growth before it OOMs again.

timeline.note: watching for 30 s with no crash or OOM
